key_insight: Modern Mixture-of-Experts models face an exploration tradeoff: adding shared experts can improve capacity, but it can also make the router less willing to try different expert combinations. This paper argues that routing exploration must be rethought to preserve the benefits of fine-grained expert segmentation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how modern MoE designs, especially shared experts plus fine-grained segmentation, can unintentionally reduce routing diversity and limit expert utilization during training.
method: Analyzes the exploration dilemma created by combining shared experts with fine-grained expert segmentation in MoE routing.
Studies how routing behavior changes when some experts are always active and how this affects token-to-expert assignment diversity.
Proposes a rethinking of routing exploration strategies to better balance expressiveness, specialization, and expert usage.
impact: This matters because better routing can improve MoE training efficiency, expert specialization, and overall model performance without simply adding more parameters. For practitioners, it offers guidance on designing MoE architectures that scale more effectively.

paper_title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
paper_authors: Bingcong Li, Hao Ma, Michael Muehlebach, Niao He, Yi Ma
